summary: Whole-roadmap target plan: imports the 197 stable targets of the two accepted parts, fills the classical/derived sheaf and nonflat décalage interfaces, and owns the canonical B_dR⁺ deformation and trace inputs needed by the semistable and Breuil–Kisin targets. The reader is the definitive consolidated specification. Imported dependency resolutions replace the older broad internal, CP.3 and RT.6 requests; they do not assert that a supplier extension is implemented. Every stage is planned with precisely recorded supplier contracts and mathematical gaps. No stage is claimed closed.

nodes.title: Flat cyclotomic power-series specialization
nodes.statement: For j≥0, the continuous map Z_p[[T]]→A_inf, T↦[ε^(1/p^j)]−1, is faithfully flat. The criterion used is BMS1 Remark 4.31: a map A→B of p-adically complete p-torsion-free rings is flat when A is noetherian and A/p→B/p is flat. Only the displayed cyclotomic maps are exported here; this is not a claim that all maps of perfectoid rings are flat.
hypotheses: p prime; C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p; O_C its valuation ring.
A_inf=W(O_C^flat), theta, phi, xi, mu and tilde-xi have the normalization of AI.0. No noetherianity of O_C or A_inf is assumed.
A compatible primitive system ε is fixed. Completeness on A_inf is for (p,[ε^(1/p^j)]−1).
proofSteps: Modulo p, use the injective map F_p[[T]]→O_C^flat and torsion-freeness over the DVR F_p[[T]]. The image of T is a nonzero nonunit.
Z_p[[T]] is noetherian, and it and A_inf are p-adically complete and p-torsion-free. Apply BMS1 Remark 4.31 to the flat map modulo p. The map is local, so flatness is faithful.
acceptance: For j=0 the map sends T to mu, and p,T remain a regular sequence.
Use faithful flatness for descent of an isomorphism, not for replacing derived scalar extension by an arbitrary degreewise tensor.

nodes.title: Nonflat quotient base change for décalage
nodes.statement: Let f and g be nonzerodivisors in A. If every H^i(K⊗^L_A A/f) has no nonzero g-torsion, the natural map (Lη_f K)⊗^L_A A/g→Lη_f(K⊗^L_A A/g) is an equivalence. On the right f denotes its image and décalage is computed on representatives on which division is defined. The condition concerns derived reduction of K, not just H^i(K)/f.

The f-décalage on A/g has its usual invertible-ideal interpretation where required by the application; in CK applications (f,g) is the specified regular coefficient pair.
proofSteps: Compare the two complexes on termwise-flat representatives.

nodes.title: Finite infinitesimal Tate thickenings
nodes.statement: For n≥1 a complete Tate B_dR⁺/ξ^n-algebra B is topologically of finite type iff B/ξ is topologically of finite type over C. Such B is strongly noetherian and every ideal is closed. A p-complete p-torsion-free A_inf/ξ^n-algebra B_0 of topologically finite type is coherent; any ideal I with B_0/I p-torsion-free is finitely generated. Its p-localization is a topologically finite-type Tate algebra, and every B as above admits such a ring of definition. Strong noetherianity means noetherianity after adjoining each finite set of Tate variables.
hypotheses: p prime; C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p; O_C its valuation ring.
A_inf=W(O_C^flat), theta, phi, xi, mu and tilde-xi have the normalization of AI.0. No noetherianity of O_C or A_inf is assumed.
Use the common B_dR⁺ complete DVR, uniformizer ξ, residue map to C and finite-quotient Tate topology; these come from R06.1 and AI.0:period-comparison.
n≥1; finite type always means topological finite type for the displayed Tate or p-adic topology.
proofSteps: Induct on n through square-zero ξ-extensions of the Tate C-algebra. Adjoining more Tate variables proves the strong form.

For integral rings use coherent square-zero extension and bounded ξ-torsion. Construct a ring of definition as the image of A_inf/ξ^n⟨X_i⟩, then use finite generation of I∩B_0 to prove closedness of I.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal envelope of a very small affinoid
nodes.statement: For very small R and Σ put P_Σ=lim_n(B_dR⁺/ξ^n)⟨X_u^{±1}:u∈Σ⟩, with e_Σ:P_Σ→R sending X_u to u. Define D_Σ(R)=lim_m P_Σ/(ker e_Σ)^m with the induced inverse-limit topology. The commuting logarithmic derivations ∂_u=X_u∂/∂X_u extend continuously; their cohomological Koszul complex is denoted Ω^•_{D_Σ(R)/B_dR⁺}. This is completion at the full embedding ideal, including the relations between the coordinates. It is not merely ξ-completion of P_Σ.

nodes.statement: A proper smooth rigid X/C is a C-valued fibre of a proper smooth morphism of smooth rigid spaces over a complete discretely valued subfield K⊂C with the same residue field. The formal input is: for complete noetherian local (W,m), an m-complete local W-algebra O with zero-dimensional O/mO and residue k, every proper flat adic formal X_O/O descends to a proper flat adic formal X_R over a complete noetherian local W-algebra R with residue k and a map R→O. Smoothness is obtained by shrinking only after proper flat descent.

Take the inverse limit of the compatible isomorphisms; use proper formal models and generic fibres for rigid spreading. Smoothness is open and allows shrinking the parameter base.

nodes.statement: For proper smooth X/C, every H^i(K_dR⁺(X)) is finite free over B_dR⁺ and vanishes outside a bounded range. Base change to C commutes with cohomology and recovers H^i_dR(X/C). If X=X_0⊗̂_K C with X_0/K proper smooth and K complete discretely valued with perfect residue field, the canonical identification is H^i(K_dR⁺(X))≃H^i_dR(X_0/K)⊗_K B_dR⁺ through the continuous lift K→B_dR⁺.

A_inf=W(O_C^flat), theta, phi, xi, mu and tilde-xi have the normalization of AI.0. No noetherianity of O_C or A_inf is assumed.
Use the common B_dR⁺ complete DVR, uniformizer ξ, residue map to C and finite-quotient Tate topology; these come from R06.1 and AI.0:period-comparison.
X proper smooth; the descended identification has the additional hypotheses on X_0 and K.
proofSteps: Spread X over a smooth affinoid base A and lift the C-valued point into B_dR⁺.
Relative proper de Rham cohomology has an integrable connection and is locally free on the smooth characteristic-zero base. Compare its coefficient extension with K_dR⁺ modulo ξ and use completeness.
Finite projective modules over the DVR B_dR⁺ are free. The descended K case is the same construction through its unique continuous lift.
acceptance: For the point the rank is one in degree zero.
A general perfect complex over a DVR can have torsion cohomology; the connection/spreading argument is required.

nodes.title: Canonical deformation-to-étale map
nodes.statement: For very small R and Σ, adjoin compatible p-power roots of all its unit coordinates. The resulting perfectoid pro-finite-étale tower has Γ=∏_{u∈Σ}Z_p(1). The degree-zero map D_Σ(R)→B_dR⁺(R_∞,Σ) sends X_u to [u^flat]. Comparing the logarithmic de Rham and continuous Γ-Koszul complexes with the normalized logarithmic operators defines a map K_dR⁺(X)→RΓ_proet(X,B_dR,X⁺). It is independent of Σ and the chosen roots after the common-envelope maps; for proper X the target is RΓ_et(X,Z_p)⊗^L B_dR⁺ by the early primitive comparison.
hypotheses: p prime; C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p; O_C its valuation ring.

R is a smooth complete Tate C-algebra. It is very small: finite units T_1,…,T_d∈Σ⊂(R°)× give a surjection C⟨X_u^{±1}:u∈Σ⟩→R, and the T_i map to the torus factors as rational embeddings and a finite étale map. Σ may be enlarged.
The root tower and continuous cochain/Koszul comparison are imported from the corrected site and AI.1.
The local operator normalization uses t=log([ε]) in B_dR⁺, a unit multiple of ξ. Rational period-sheaf acyclicity is supplied by P8:local-rational, not used to construct the integral AI.3 sheaf.
proofSteps: Extend the coordinate Teichmüller map through the embedding-ideal completion.

On the common envelope, Γ acts by exp(t∂_u). The divided operator (exp(t∂_u)−1)/∂_u is interpreted as t∑_{n≥0}t^n∂_u^n/(n+1)!, with no inverse derivation. Products of these commuting operators give the degree-indexed Koszul chain map.
Use the all-coordinate transition maps to glue. The local map identifies the de Rham complex with η_ξ of the period Koszul complex; after ξ-inversion décalage is the identity.
acceptance: The degree-zero coordinate map and all higher normalizations belong to the same comparison.
An isomorphism of abstract free modules is not a substitute for this canonical map.

nodes.title: Relative cyclotomic traces over the sphere polynomial ring
nodes.statement: Let 𝕊[z]=𝕊[ℕ] be the monoid-algebra sphere spectrum, not the free E∞-ring on a degree-zero element. For a connective E∞-𝕊[z]-algebra A, define THH(A) by the cyclic bar realization and THH(A/𝕊[z])=THH(A)⊗_{THH(𝕊[z])}𝕊[z]. It is a circle-equivariant E∞-algebra. The cyclic bar B^cyℕ has weight-zero point and positive-weight circles with t·(s,n)=(t^n s,n). The cyclotomic map comes from (s,n)↦(s^p,pn), the absolute cyclotomic map and lax monoidality of the finite-group Tate construction. It is semilinear for z↦z^p. Define TC⁻(A/𝕊[z];Z_p)=THH(A/𝕊[z])^{h𝕋} and TP(A/𝕊[z];Z_p)=THH(A/𝕊[z])^{t𝕋}, with canonical map can and cyclotomic Frobenius phi. These two maps have different coefficient normalizations.
hypotheses: p is prime. Work in the symmetric monoidal stable enhancement of spectra, with E∞-algebras, geometric realizations, circle actions, homotopy fixed points and Tate constructions supplied by the precise E5:abstract contract.
All displayed trace invariants are p-completed; homotopy indices are homological, so the Bott generator has degree +2.
A has the specified 𝕊[z]-algebra structure. The cyclotomic target circle action uses 𝕋≅𝕋/C_p, not the unchanged residual action.
proofSteps: Realize the cyclic bar of an E∞-algebra in spectra to obtain THH and its circle action. The needed stable spectral and norm/Tate operations are the supplier extension G-TRACE-FOUNDATIONS, not ordinary derived-category operations at the pin.
Compute the monoid cyclic bar weightwise. The square relating its augmentation to z↦z^p allows the relative tensor product to inherit the cyclotomic map by Construction 11.5.
Take circle homotopy fixed points and the circle Tate construction; the canonical and Frobenius maps are induced separately.
acceptance: The spectral base has π_*𝕊[z]=π_*𝕊[z]; a free E∞ generator would have symmetric-group homotopy and fail this description.
Relative traces remain circle-equivariant and Frobenius-semilinear for z^p throughout base change.

nodes.title: Perfectoid trace coefficient calculation
nodes.statement: For an integral perfectoid R with A_inf(R), one can choose a theta-kernel generator ξ and compatible degree-two generators, with tilde-ξ=phi(ξ), such that π_*THH(R;Z_p)=R[b], π_*TC⁻(R;Z_p)=A_inf(R)[b,v]/(bv−ξ), and π_*TP(R;Z_p)=A_inf(R)[σ^{±1}], with |b|=|σ|=2 and |v|=−2. can is A_inf-linear with b↦ξσ, v↦σ^−1; phi is semilinear for Witt Frobenius with b↦σ, v↦tilde-ξ σ^−1. For connective E∞-R-algebras A, quotient by v gives THH(A;Z_p), while the TP quotient by tilde-ξ gives THH(A;Z_p)^{tC_p}. These formulas use a compatible choice of ξ as well as the graded generators; they do not assert simultaneous normalization for an arbitrary preassigned ξ or a canonical basis of a Tate line.

R integral perfectoid, with its primitive theta-kernel generator and the coefficient identification from P1/PR.0.
proofSteps: The perfectoid completed cotangent calculation gives the HKR filtration. The Bökstedt calculation for F_p and perfectoid base change give the polynomial THH coefficients; the source uses a pseudocoherence/Nakayama induction.

Use the homotopy fixed point and Tate spectral sequences to identify the ξ-adic thickening with A_inf by its universal property. Normalize the generators so phi(b)=σ, then multiplicativity determines phi(v).
Use the perfect TC⁻-module quotient by v to identify the connective algebra base-change squares. The F_p Bökstedt calculation remains an explicit spectral supplier input.
acceptance: The canonical and Frobenius maps send bv to ξ and tilde-ξ respectively.
For characteristic-p perfect R, ξ=p; the formula reduces to the Witt coefficient calculation.

nodes.title: Quasisyntomic unfolding of the trace coefficient sheaf
nodes.statement: For quasiregular semiperfectoid S over a perfectoid R, put D̂_S=π_0TC⁻(S;Z_p)≃π_0TP(S;Z_p). The spectral sequences are even; multiplication by v^i identifies π_{2i}TC⁻ with the complete descending Nygaard level N^{≥i}D̂_S, with gr_N^iD̂_S≃π_{2i}THH for i≥0. The cohomology groups form acyclic sheaves on the quasiregular semiperfectoid basis. Unfold these sheaves to the quasisyntomic site and define gr^0TC⁻=gr^0TP as D̂_A. For a general A this unfolded object is a derived complex, not π_0TC⁻(A). Its coherent multiplicative filtration and coefficient twists are retained.
hypotheses: p is prime. Work in the symmetric monoidal stable enhancement of spectra, with E∞-algebras, geometric realizations, circle actions, homotopy fixed points and Tate constructions supplied by the precise E5:abstract contract.
All displayed trace invariants are p-completed; homotopy indices are homological, so the Bott generator has degree +2.
S quasiregular semiperfectoid; A quasisyntomic and p-complete with bounded p-torsion as in BMS2.
The quasisyntomic site, its quasiregular semiperfectoid basis and symmetric monoidal sheaf-unfolding equivalence are supplied by PR.3 and E2.
proofSteps: Use the quasiregular cotangent-amplitude calculation and THH/HKR filtration to prove evenness and the p-complete flatness of the homotopy groups.
The fixed-point/Tate spectral sequences degenerate; read the v^i filtration and use flat descent of derived exterior powers to prove sheaf acyclicity.
Apply the symmetric monoidal unfolding equivalence on the basis (BMS2 Proposition 4.31). Recover the complete multiplicative filtered complex, not a chosen cochain model.
acceptance: On a quasiregular semiperfectoid basis object D̂ is discrete and agrees with π_0TP.
On a smooth torus the unfolded object has higher cohomology and cannot be replaced by an unproved discrete π_0 object.

nodes.title: Characteristic-p trace and crystalline comparison
nodes.statement: For a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra S, the trace D̂_S is naturally the Nygaard completion of its derived de Rham–Witt/crystalline complex, preserving the Nygaard filtration. Cyclotomic Frobenius agrees with the functorial Frobenius of S and lifts the mod-p Frobenius. By descent, for a smooth algebra A over a perfect field k this gives the de Rham–Witt/crystalline trace comparison. The separate Segal input is: for A smooth of dimension d, THH(A)→THH(A)^{tC_p} is the connective truncation in degrees ≥d, in the precise degree-by-degree form of BMS2 Corollary 8.18; it yields the stable-range Frobenius used by Proposition 11.15. More precisely gr^iTHH(A)≃(τ^{≤i}Ω^•_{A/k})[2i] and gr^iTHH(A)^{tC_p}≃Ω^•_{A/k}[2i], and the map is the truncation inclusion; hence the whole map is an equivalence in homotopy degrees ≥d.

Use the universal PD envelope and extend the map to Nygaard completions, then descend to smooth A. Keep the distinction between the cyclotomic and ring-induced Frobenius until agreement is proved.
Apply the THH filtration and characteristic-p Frobenius calculation in the range ≥d to obtain the Segal connective truncation. The exact threshold is checked separately when applying Bott inversion.

nodes.title: Relative Breuil–Kisin trace coefficients
nodes.statement: For O_K, the p-completed relative coefficients are π_*THH=O_K[b], π_*TC⁻=𝔖^(−1)[b,v]/(bv−E), and π_*TP=𝔖^(−1)[σ^{±1}], with |b|=|σ|=2 and |v|=−2. can sends b↦Eσ and v↦σ^−1, linearly on 𝔖^(−1); phi acts by Witt Frobenius/u^p on coefficients and sends b↦σ, v↦phi(E)σ^−1. The Tate target of relative THH has coefficients O_K[π^{1/p}][σ^{±1}]; its coefficient map evaluates u at π^{1/p}, rather than π. These equalities use the relative sphere-polynomial construction, not absolute THH(O_K).
hypotheses: p is prime. Work in the symmetric monoidal stable enhancement of spectra, with E∞-algebras, geometric realizations, circle actions, homotopy fixed points and Tate constructions supplied by the precise E5:abstract contract.
All displayed trace invariants are p-completed; homotopy indices are homological, so the Bott generator has degree +2.
K is a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k; π is a fixed uniformizer with Eisenstein polynomial E over W(k).

𝔖=W(k)[[u]], phi acts by Witt Frobenius and u↦u^p. 𝔖^(−1) is a copy of 𝔖 regarded as a 𝔖-algebra along phi. In the spectral sphere-polynomial base use a separate variable z↦π; in coefficient formulas u is the power-series variable and b is the degree-two class.
proofSteps: Base change along the perfectoid root base reduces the computation to the perfectoid coefficient theorem.
Identify π_0 with the Frobenius-shifted copy of 𝔖 and choose compatible generators. Multiplicativity forces the two formulas on v from the relation bv=E.
Track theta^(−1) and tilde-theta^(−1) in the square with THH and its finite Tate construction.
acceptance: can(bv)=E, whereas phi(bv)=phi(E).
The target quotient evaluation u↦π^{1/p} distinguishes tilde-theta from theta in this trace diagram.

nodes.title: Relative quasiregular evenness and descent
nodes.statement: For S a quasiregular semiperfectoid quasisyntomic O_K-algebra, the relative THH, TC⁻ and TP spectra over 𝕊[z] have no odd homotopy. Each homotopy group is an acyclic sheaf on the quasiregular semiperfectoid basis. π_0TC⁻≃π_0TP unfolds to an E∞-𝔖^(−1)-algebra D̂_{A/𝔖^(−1)} on QSyn_{O_K}, with the complete descending multiplicative Nygaard filtration from the homotopy fixed point spectral sequence. For smooth A this is the twisted trace complex of the imported AI.7 target; its specializations are those of Corollary 11.12, including the identity Witt map and u↦π on 𝔖^(−1).

proofSteps: After p-completed base change to O_{K_∞}, apply absolute quasiregular evenness and descent; coefficient extension is topologically free and detects the needed assertions.

nodes.title: Bott inversion and Frobenius descent input
nodes.statement: The relative cyclotomic Frobenius extends naturally from TC⁻ to TC⁻[1/b]⊗_{𝕊[z]}𝕊[z^{1/p}]→TP because phi(b)=σ is invertible. For quasiregular semiperfectoid A, the Bott-localized source remains even with acyclic homotopy sheaves. After unfolding degree zero, the extended map is an equivalence for A the p-adic completion of a smooth O_K-algebra. This is the Frobenius-descent input defining the untwisted Breuil–Kisin complex in the imported trace-descent target. No Bott inversion of the power-series parameter u is intended.

nodes.title: Regularity of affinoid perfectoid coefficients
nodes.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid Spa(S[1/p],S) over Spa(C,O_C), A_inf(S)=W(S^flat) is (p,mu)-adically complete, A_inf(S)/mu is p-adically complete, and (p^n,mu^m) is a regular sequence for every n,m>0. Its quotient by this sequence is flat over A_inf/(p^n,mu^m). Theta is surjective with kernel generated by the image of xi. The coefficient ring is xi-adically separated. These assertions apply to the chart and all-coordinate towers; they are not asserted for an arbitrary p-complete algebra.
hypotheses: p prime; C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p; O_C its valuation ring.
A_inf=W(O_C^flat), theta, phi, xi, mu and tilde-xi have the normalization of AI.0. No noetherianity of O_C or A_inf is assumed.
S is the integral ring in the stated affinoid perfectoid pair; S^flat has no nonzero O_C^flat-torsion.
proofSteps: Use torsion-freeness of S^flat over the valuation ring O_C^flat, the Witt reduction modulo p, and regular-sequence dévissage to get regularity and finite-quotient flatness.

The Witt coordinate topology proves (p,mu)-completeness; the finite Witt theta sequences prove p-completeness after mod mu. Apply the ideal-completeness/separatedness criterion to xi in the radical of (p,mu).
acceptance: At S=O_C this specializes to the coefficient-ring regularity target.
Flatness is stated for the finite quotients; no unrestricted completed-tensor exactness follows.

nodes.title: Derived-reduction almost-to-integral criterion
nodes.statement: If b:B→B′ in D(A_inf) has W(m^flat)-annihilated cone cohomology and every H^i(B⊗^L A_inf/mu) has no nonzero W(m^flat)-annihilated element, then Lη_mu(b) is an equivalence. This criterion uses the source derived reduction; it does not identify Lη of a cone with the cone of Lη.
hypotheses: p prime; C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p; O_C its valuation ring.
A_inf=W(O_C^flat), theta, phi, xi, mu and tilde-xi have the normalization of AI.0. No noetherianity of O_C or A_inf is assumed.
Both conditions hold in every cohomological degree. W(m^flat) is the Witt residue-kernel ideal, without an idempotence assumption.
proofSteps: Derived mod-mu reduction gives the short exact sequence of Bockstein complexes in CK proof 3.18, using the source no-almost-zero hypothesis.
The mod-mu cone of Lη_mu(b) vanishes. Thus mu acts invertibly on its cohomology. After mu-localization b is already an equivalence because mu belongs to W(m^flat); conclude that the cone vanishes.
acceptance: Do not invoke exactness of Lη as a triangulated functor.
Almostness alone, without the derived-reduction source hypothesis, is insufficient.

nodes.title: Continuous cohomology of completed coefficient sums
nodes.statement: Let H be profinite, i≥0 and M_j p-adically complete p-torsion-free continuous H-modules. If either every H^i_cont(H,M_j) is p-torsion-free, or a single p^n annihilates them all, the coordinate map H^i_cont(H,⊕̂_j M_j)→∏_j H^i_cont(H,M_j) is injective. Consequently the completed-sum cohomology is respectively p-torsion-free or killed by that same p^n. Completion is p-adic and the bound is uniform in j.
hypotheses: The topology on ⊕̂_j M_j is the completed direct-sum topology; all actions are continuous.
The alternatives and p-torsion-freeness of the coefficient modules are part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Write a cocycle coordinatewise. Its coordinate p-adic orders tend to infinity.
Choose primitives at those orders, or with the fixed loss n in the bounded-torsion case. The primitives still tend to zero and form a cochain in the completed sum.
acceptance: A nonuniform family of exponents cannot be used to conclude one fixed annihilator.
This is injectivity into a product, not surjectivity or a claim of commutation with an arbitrary direct sum.

nodes.title: Normalized length over a rank-one valuation ring
nodes.statement: For a rank-one mixed-characteristic valuation ring V with additive valuation val(p)=1 and a finitely presented torsion V-module M≃⊕_i V/(a_i), a_i≠0, define val_V(M)=Σ_i val(a_i). Equivalently take the valuation of a generator of Fitt_0(M). This is independent of presentation, additive on short exact sequences of finitely presented torsion modules, and invariant under valuation-preserving scalar extension. For V a DVR with p uniformizer it is ordinary module length. A free summand is outside this finite-length domain.
hypotheses: V rank one, characteristic zero, residue characteristic p; val is additive and normalized at p.
M finitely presented and torsion; scalar extensions preserve the normalized valuation.
proofSteps: Apply the elementary-divisor structure theorem over a valuation ring. Relate the product of the a_i to Fitt_0(M).

The Fitting-ideal multiplicativity theorem for these torsion presentations proves additivity; extending the diagonal presentation proves scalar-extension invariance. Both algebraic results are the supplier extension G-LENGTH.
acceptance: Use the same normalization on O_C, W(C^flat) and Z_p.
An ordinary integer-valued composition length over nondiscrete O_C is not substituted.

api.name: AInf.normalized_valuation_length.cyclic
api.statement: For nonzero a∈V, val_V(V/(a))=val(a); if a is a unit this is zero.

api.name: AInf.normalized_valuation_length.exact
api.statement: An exact sequence 0→M_1→M_2→M_3→0 in the stated domain gives val_V(M_2)=val_V(M_1)+val_V(M_3).

api.name: AInf.normalized_valuation_length.base_change
api.statement: For a valuation-preserving extension V→V′, val_V′(M⊗V′)=val_V(M).

api.statement: If Fitt_0(M)=(a), then val_V(M)=val(a), so the definition is intrinsic.

nodes.title: Finite-Witt valuation-length specialization identity
nodes.statement: For n≥1 and M finitely presented over W_n(O_C^flat), val_{W(C^flat)}(M⊗_{A_inf}W(C^flat))=val_{O_C}(M/xi M)−val_{O_C}(M[xi]). Both right-hand modules are finitely presented torsion modules. The target over W(C^flat) uses p normalized to one. This identity includes the xi-Tor correction and underlies the semistable de Rham torsion inequalities.

proofSteps: Coherence gives finite presentation of the xi-torsion. Both expressions are additive on finite-p-level short exact sequences by the snake lemma and normalized length.

The existing node completed-sheaf-tensor is a bifunctor over one ring on a replete topos and supplies neither.

The category of BMS1 Definition 4.1 and BMS2 Definition 1.1: finitely generated 𝔖-modules M with an isomorphism (φ_𝔖^*M)[1/E]≅M[1/E], with BMS1 Proposition 4.3 (structure 0→M_tor→M→M_free→M̄→0 and M[1/p] finite free over 𝔖[1/p]). gaps.title: Formal GAGA and coherent finiteness over a rank-one valuation ring
gaps.detail: Three statements about a proper formal scheme over a complete rank-one valuation ring that is not noetherian. (a) CK Theorem 4.12 with Remark 4.13 (Fujiwara–Kato, Foundations of rigid geometry I, I.10.1.2): for a height-one valuation ring V complete for a nonzero nonunit a and a proper finitely presented V-scheme Y, finitely presented O_Y-modules are equivalent to compatible systems of finitely presented modules on the Y_{V/a^n}, and locally free systems algebraise to locally free modules. CK uses it once, in §4.15, to algebraise the map (4.10.3); among the nodes only hodge-tate-comparison uses it directly, and only for the identification (4.11.1). (b) The finiteness theorem for proper formal schemes over O_C (Ullrich, The direct image theorem in formal and rigid geometry, 5.3), used in CK Corollary 4.20 for proper-perfectness. (c) The comparison theorem and flat base change from O_K to O_C for coherent cohomology (EGA III 4.1.7 with limit arguments, or Fujiwara–Kato I.9.2.1), used in CK Remark 4.19 and for (8.7.4) in model-independent-lattice. CK's deductions were read; the proofs in Fujiwara–Kato and Ullrich were not. AdicSpacesPartII:F0 plans formal functions and formal GAGA for Noetherian adic rings only; the restructure entry proposes to extend it.

gaps.title: External inputs with no located supplier
gaps.detail: Named results that the proofs use and for which no stage of the atlas was found to state them. For divisorial-log and hodge-tate-comparison (CK §1.5): the algebraisation (1.5.2) of a chart and of an étale map to it over a discrete valuation subring of the integral closure of W(k̄) (Stacks Project 04D1 with limit arguments). For root-tower and structure-sheaf-edge (CK §1.5, §3.2): Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.1.6 (R is flat over R□ and each R⊗_{R□}R□_m is p-adically complete). For hodge-tate-comparison (CK §4.10, §4.15): the identification of (R¹ν_*Ô⁺)[1/p] with Ω¹(−1) on a smooth proper adic space over C (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey, 3.23–3.24); the extension of a vector bundle across a closed subset of codimension ≥2 over a non-noetherian valuation base (EGA IV₂ 5.10.5 with limit arguments); the existence of a proper flat compactification of the chart with Zariski-local semistable coordinates. For global-crystalline (CK, proof of Corollary 5.43): the descent of 𝔛_{O_C/p} to a quasi-compact quasi-separated fine log smooth log scheme of Cartier type over O/p, proper when 𝔛 is, for the ring of integers O of a finite extension of W(k̄)[1/p] in C; CK says only that limit arguments give it. For hyodo-kato-interface: base change of log crystalline cohomology of a fine, log smooth log scheme of Cartier type along W(k₀)→W(k̄) (identification (iii) of the node), which CK does not state; it is requested from CR.6, and whether Beilinson's (1.11.1) covers it was not checked. For local-crystalline and aomega-sheaf-completeness (CK, proofs of Proposition 5.13 and Corollary 4.6): acyclicity of quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine formal scheme (Fujiwara–Kato I.1.1.23(2)). For bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings and bdr-comparison-map (CK §§6.3–6.5): the reduced fibre theorem (Stacks Project 09IL), Raynaud–Gruson I.3.3.5 (freeness of A₀ over O), Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.3.15 (power-bounded elements of a nilpotent thickening) and, for bdr-comparison-map, the descent (1.5.2) of the charts. For de-rham-lattice-functor and model-independent-lattice (CK §8.5, (8.7.4)): the theorems of Ax–Sen–Tate (C^{G_K}=K, hence (O_C)^{G_K}=O_K) and of Tate and Sen ((C(η))^{G_K}=0 for a character η with infinite image on inertia) are cited from PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants and R06.1/tate-sen-theorem, which state them for K finite over Q_p; CK's K is any complete discretely valued field with perfect residue field, and that generality is the gap. Also the formalism of de Rham representations of G_K (D_dR(V)=(V⊗B_dR)^{G_K}, injectivity of D_dR(V)⊗_KB_dR→V⊗B_dR, compatibility with tensor products, duals and finite extensions), which CK uses without reference; and the G_K-equivariant identification H^i_ét(X_{K̄},Z_p)≅H^i_ét(X_C,Z_p) for X proper smooth over K. For crystalline-torsion and de-rham-torsion (second inequalities of CK Theorems 7.9 and 7.12): RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p)⊗^L Z/p^n≅RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z/p^n) and the analogous base change of log crystalline and log de Rham cohomology to W_n(k̄) and O_C/p^n, for which CK cites only the universal coefficient sequences. For nygaard-nondescent (the worked example): the j-invariant of a Weierstrass curve and its invariance under base change, and the algebraisation of a smooth proper formal curve of genus one over ℤ_p. For perfect-cohomological-modules: finiteness of the coherent cohomology of a proper scheme over a field (EGA III 3.2.1), hence of its de Rham cohomology.

gaps.title: Coherent cohomology of the nodal conic
gaps.detail: The node nodal-conic computes the log de Rham groups O_K, 0, O_K of the completed conic XY=πZ² from H⁰(O)=O_K, H¹(O)=0, H⁰(ω)=0, H¹(ω)≅O_K, where ω=Ω¹_log is the relative dualizing sheaf. Compute the log de Rham cohomology directly. Ω¹_log of 𝔛₀ over O_K is an invertible sheaf, generated at the node by dlog x=−dlog y and on the two smooth charts by the differential of the coordinate; it is the relative dualizing sheaf ω (CR.5). The special fibre is the union of two lines L₁, L₂ over k₀ meeting in one point: the sequence 0→O→O_{L₁}⊕O_{L₂}→k₀→0 gives H⁰(O)=k₀ and H¹(O)=0, and ω restricts to O(−1) on each line, so H⁰(ω)=0 and, by duality, H¹(ω)=k₀. The generic fibre is P¹_K and has the same dimensions, so by cohomology and base change for the proper flat curve H⁰(O)=O_K, H¹(O)=0, H⁰(ω)=0 and H¹(ω)≅O_K. The Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence then has E₁^{0,1}=E₁^{1,0}=0, and the log de Rham groups are O_K, 0, O_K in degrees 0, 1, 2. The inputs of this step (the normalization exact sequence for the two components, Serre duality, cohomology and base change, and the identification of Ω¹_log with ω) have no supplier among the prerequisites.

Apply freeness-criterion and degreewise-specializations for the freeness and the ranks of the A_inf groups. Apply model-independent-lattice, (8.7.3), in degrees 0 and 2, and the cases M(Z_p)=A_inf and M(Z_p(−1))=A_inf{−1} of de-rham-lattice-functor (its trivial and Tate-twist computations; A_inf{−1} is AI.2’s Tate twist) to identify the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues structures; degree 3 vanishes, so the hypothesis on degree i+1 holds for i=2. The common lattices are L⁰_dR(P¹_K)=O_K and L²_dR(P¹_K)=L_dR(Z_p(−1))=O_K·(t⊗ε^∨).

fields.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over C. (1) Étale topology (CK §6.2). The analytic, respectively étale, topology of X has a basis of affinoids Spa(A,A°) that admit a map to a torus Spa(C⟨T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}⟩,O_C⟨T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}⟩) which is a composite of a rational embedding, a finite étale map and a rational embedding, and a finite set Ψ⊂(A°)^× with C⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ}⟩→A, X_u↦u, surjective. For such data put B_dR⁺⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ}⟩=lim_n (B_dR⁺/ξⁿ)⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ}⟩, let s be its surjection onto A, D_Ψ(A)=lim_n B_dR⁺⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ}⟩/(Ker s)ⁿ, let Ω^•_{D_Ψ(A)/B_dR⁺} be the Koszul complex of the commuting derivations ∂/∂log X_u=X_u·∂/∂X_u of D_Ψ(A), and Ω^•_{A/B_dR⁺}=colim_Ψ Ω^•_{D_Ψ(A)/B_dR⁺}. Let RΓ_crys(X/B_dR⁺), respectively RΓ_crys(X_ét/B_dR⁺), be the hypercohomology of the associated complex of sheaves for the analytic, respectively étale, topology; the first agrees with the complex of BMS1 §13 supplied by AI.6 canonical deformation. Then both are derived ξ-adically complete (6.2.5); their reductions modulo ξ are canonically and compatibly identified with RΓ(X,Ω^{•,cont}_{X/C})=RΓ_dR(X/C) and RΓ(X_ét,Ω^{•,cont}_{X/C}) (6.2.6); and pullback is an isomorphism RΓ_crys(X/B_dR⁺)≃RΓ_crys(X_ét/B_dR⁺) (6.2.7). (2) Non-unit coordinates (CK §§6.3–6.4). The étale topology of X has a basis of affinoids Spa(A,A°) with the following data: an étale map (6.3.1) to Spa(C⟨T_0,…,T_r,T_{r+1}^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}⟩/(T_0⋯T_r−p^q), O_C⟨T_0,…,T_r,T_{r+1}^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}⟩/(T_0⋯T_r−p^q)) for some d≥r≥0 and q∈Q_{>0}; a finite extension K of W(k̄)[1/p] in C with ring of integers O∋p^q and a finite type O[T_0,…,T_r,T_{r+1}^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}]/(T_0⋯T_r−p^q)-algebra A_0, étale after inverting p, O-flat, normal, with no connected component of Spec A_0 on which p is a unit, such that (6.3.1) is the base change to C of an étale map (6.3.2) from Spa(Â_0[1/p],Â_0) and A_0⊗̂_O O_C≃A° (6.3.3); and finite sets Ψ_0⊂(Â_0)^×, Ξ_0⊂Â_0∩(Â_0[1/p])^× with K⟨(x_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ_0},(x_a)_{a∈Ξ_0}⟩→Â_0[1/p] surjective (6.3.4). For finite Ψ⊂(A°)^× and Ξ⊂A°∩A^× with C⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ},(X_a)_{a∈Ξ}⟩→A surjective (6.3.5), let D_{Ψ,Ξ,n}(A)=B_dR⁺⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ},(X_a)_{a∈Ξ}⟩/(Ker s)ⁿ, D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)=lim_n D_{Ψ,Ξ,n}(A), and let Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺} be the Koszul complex of the derivations ∂/∂log X_a, a∈Ψ∪Ξ. Let B_dR⁺⊗̂_K A_0[1/p]=lim_n(((B_dR⁺/ξⁿ)_0⊗̂_O A_0)[1/p]), where (B_dR⁺/ξⁿ)_0 is the A_inf/ξⁿ-subalgebra of B_dR⁺/ξⁿ generated by the image of O; it has no ξ-torsion, is ξ-adically complete and reduces to A modulo ξ (6.3.6). (a) Lemma 6.3.8: suppose that Ψ, respectively Ξ, contains the images of the T_i for r+1≤i≤d, respectively 1≤i≤r, under a coordinate map (6.3.1), and that Ψ and Ξ are large enough in the sense of CK §6.4, namely: for some choice of (Ψ_0,Ξ_0) as in (6.3.4) such that Ψ_0, respectively Ξ_0, contains the images of the T_i for r+1≤i≤d, respectively 1≤i≤r, under (6.3.2), Ψ contains the image of Ψ_0 in A° and Ξ contains the image of Ξ_0. Then D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)≃(B_dR⁺⊗̂_K A_0[1/p])[[(X_a−ã)_{a∈(Ψ∪Ξ)∖{T_1,…,T_d}}]] (6.3.9), where ã is a fixed lift of a in lim_n((B_dR⁺/ξⁿ)_0⊗̂_O A_0); in particular D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A) has no nonzero ξ-torsion and is ξ-adically complete. (b) For such Ψ and Ξ, Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺}/ξ≃Ω^{•,cont}_{A/C} in the derived category, compatibly with enlarging Ψ and Ξ (6.3.10), and for Ψ′⊇Ψ, Ξ′⊇Ξ the map Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺}→Ω^•_{D_{Ψ′,Ξ′}(A)/B_dR⁺} is a quasi-isomorphism. (c) If Spa(A,A°) also belongs to the basis of (1), the map Ω^•_{A/B_dR⁺}→colim_{Ψ,Ξ}Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺} is a quasi-isomorphism, functorial in Spa(A,A°) (6.3.11). Such affinoids form a basis of X_ét, so the hypercohomology of the sheafification of Spa(A,A°)↦colim_{Ψ,Ξ}Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺} is RΓ_crys(X_ét/B_dR⁺)≃RΓ_crys(X/B_dR⁺), and under this identification the maps (6.3.10) recover (6.2.6) ((6.3.12)). No multiplicative structure on these complexes is asserted.
proofSteps: Bases for part (1): by Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces, 1.6.10 and 2.2.8, the analytic and the étale topology of X have bases of affinoids with coordinate maps (6.2.1); localising further gives the surjections (6.2.2). Huber’s results are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1.

By BMS1 Lemma 13.12(ii) and Lemma 13.13 (AI.6 canonical deformation), for fixed Spa(A,A°) and Ψ large, D_Ψ(A) is ξ-torsion-free and ξ-adically complete, Ω^•_{D_Ψ(A)/B_dR⁺}→Ω^•_{A/B_dR⁺} is a quasi-isomorphism and Ω^•_{D_Ψ(A)/B_dR⁺}/ξ≃Ω^{•,cont}_{A/C}. By BMS1 Lemma 9.15 (AI.6 canonical deformation; for the étale site its analogue, as in the proof of CK Corollary 4.6), the definition with sheafification agrees with that of BMS1 §13, both complexes are derived ξ-complete (6.2.5), and their reductions modulo ξ are the de Rham complexes (6.2.6).

(6.2.7): by the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence and Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Proposition 9.2(ii) (coherent cohomology is the same in the analytic and in the étale topology; AdicSpacesPartII:R3), RΓ(X,Ω^{•,cont}_{X/C})→RΓ(X_ét,Ω^{•,cont}_{X/C}) is an isomorphism. Both sides of (6.2.7) are derived ξ-complete and the pullback map is an isomorphism modulo ξ, hence an isomorphism.

Descent for part (2): by Huber 1.7.3 iii) and limit arguments, (6.3.1) descends to (6.3.2) over a finite extension K of W(k̄)[1/p]; by the reduced fibre theorem (Stacks Project 09IL) K can be enlarged so that (6.3.3) holds. By BMS1 Lemma 13.4(ii) (AI.6 canonical deformation) each D_{Ψ,Ξ,n}(A) is a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring, with the image of (A_inf/ξⁿ)⟨(X_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ},(X_a)_{a∈Ξ}⟩ as a ring of definition. By the proof of BMS1 Lemma 13.11, which simplifies here because A_0 is a free O-module (Raynaud–Gruson, Critères de platitude et de projectivité, I.3.3.5, and Stacks Project 0593), the ring B_dR⁺⊗̂_K A_0[1/p] is ξ-torsion-free and ξ-adically complete with reduction A, and lim_n((B_dR⁺/ξⁿ)_0⊗̂_O A_0) surjects onto A° ((6.3.6), (6.3.7)). The K-algebra structure of B_dR⁺ is AI.0:period-comparison’s.

Lemma 6.3.8 (CK §6.4, adapting BMS1 Lemma 13.12(ii)): put D_{0,n}=K⟨(x_u^{±1})_{u∈Ψ_0},(x_a)_{a∈Ξ_0}⟩/(Ker s_0)ⁿ and D_0=lim_n D_{0,n}. Since A_0[1/p] is étale over K[T_1,…,T_r,T_{r+1}^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}], the map A_0[1/p]→Â_0[1/p] lifts to A_0[1/p]→D_0 with T_i↦x_{T_i} ((6.4.1)). By Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.3.15, the power-bounded elements of D_{0,n} are the preimage of those of Â_0[1/p], so A_0 maps into a ring of definition; composing with D_{0,n}→D_{Ψ,Ξ,n}(A) gives a continuous map y from the right side of (6.3.9) to D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A). A continuous map z in the other direction is defined from X_{T_i}↦T_i, the expansion X_u^{−1}=ũ^{−1}(1−ũ^{−1}(X_u−ũ)+…) for u∈Ψ and ξ-adic completeness. Then y∘z=id by construction and z∘y=id by étaleness, so z is the isomorphism (6.3.9).

(6.3.10) and enlargement: every a∈Ψ∪Ξ is a unit of A, so the proof of BMS1 Lemma 13.13 gives Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺}/ξ≃Ω^{•,cont}_{A/C}, compatibly with enlarging Ψ and Ξ; by the ξ-completeness and ξ-torsion-freeness of Lemma 6.3.8 the enlargement maps are quasi-isomorphisms.

(6.3.11) and (6.3.12): for Spa(A,A°) in both bases, D_Ψ(A)=D_{Ψ,∅}(A), and the map from colim_Ψ to colim_{Ψ,Ξ} is a quasi-isomorphism because for large indices both sides are computed by ξ-torsion-free, ξ-complete terms with the same reduction modulo ξ (CK state (6.3.11) as a consequence without further argument). The affinoids with r=0 already form a basis of X_ét, so sheafifying gives RΓ_crys(X_ét/B_dR⁺), and (6.2.7) gives (6.3.12).

fields.statement: Let 𝔛 be as in CK §1.5; its adic generic fibre X_C^ad is then smooth over C. Let RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺) be AI.6 canonical deformation’s B_dR⁺-cohomology (BMS1 §13), computed in the étale topology with the rings D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A) of bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings. For an affine Spf R in 𝔛_ét with all-coordinates data (Σ,Λ) as in CK §5.17, put A=R[1/p], Ξ=⋃_{λ∈Λ}{t_{λ,1},…,t_{λ,r_λ}} and Ψ={t_σ}_{σ∈Σ}∪⋃_{λ∈Λ}{t_{λ,r_λ+1},…,t_{λ,d}}, enlarged by the images of the units Ψ₀ obtained by descending the closed immersion (5.17.2) to a finite extension of W(k̄)[1/p]; the coordinates t_{λ,0} are omitted. CK §6.5 constructs continuous ring maps D_{Σ,Λ}→D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A) over A_cris→B_dR⁺ (6.5.5), independent of the auxiliary chart λ₀, compatible with the maps to R[1/p] and with the logarithmic derivations ∂/∂log X_σ and ∂/∂log X_{λ,i}, 1≤i≤d. The induced maps of Koszul complexes (6.5.6) are compatible with enlarging (Σ,Λ) and (Ψ,Ξ) and with replacing R by a p-adically formally étale R-algebra; after sheafification they give the map (6.5.1) RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris)→RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺) over A_cris→B_dR⁺, hence a B_dR⁺-linear map RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris)⊗^L_{A_cris}B_dR⁺→RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺). It sits in the commutative square (6.5.7) with the reduction RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris)→RΓ_logdR(𝔛/O_C) of (5.23.2), the reduction modulo ξ of (6.2.6) and the map RΓ_logdR(𝔛/O_C)→RΓ_dR(X_C^ad/C) to the generic fibre. If 𝔛 is proper, compose with global-crystalline’s RΓ_Ainf(𝔛)⊗^L_{A_inf}A_cris≃RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris) to obtain the A_inf-to-B_dR⁺ map RΓ_Ainf(𝔛)⊗^L_{A_inf}B_dR⁺→RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺). This is a comparison to AI.6 canonical deformation’s object, not its construction. Naturality for arbitrary morphisms of models, Galois equivariance and multiplicativity of the map are not asserted.
proofSteps: The adic generic fibre X_C^ad is smooth over C by the charts (1.5.1) and Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces, 3.5.1 (CK §1.5). Import RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺) from AI.6 canonical deformation and, from bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings, its computation in the étale topology by the complexes Ω^•_{D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)/B_dR⁺} ((6.2.7), (6.3.11), (6.3.12)).

Local data (CK (6.5.2)): for Spf R with data (Σ,Λ) as in CK §5.17 (all-coordinates) set A=R[1/p], so that A°≃R, and Ψ, Ξ as in the statement. Descend the étale maps (5.17.3) to the ring of integers of a finite extension K of W(k̄)[1/p] in C (CK (1.5.2)) to obtain the descended coordinate map (6.3.2); after enlarging K, descend the closed immersion (5.17.2) to a surjection (6.3.4) with Ξ₀=∅ and adjoin the image of the resulting Ψ₀ to Ψ. Then Spa(A,A°) lies in the refined basis and Lemma 6.3.8 applies to Ψ and Ξ (bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings).

By the descent and Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.3.15, the elements [(p^{1/p^∞})^{q_λ}]/(X_{t_{λ,1}}⋯X_{t_{λ,r_λ}}) of D_{Ψ,Ξ,n}(A) are power-bounded. Hence (D_{Ψ,Ξ,n}(A))° is an algebra over the ring A□_{Σ,Λ} of (5.22.1), with X_σ↦X_{t_σ}, X_{λ,i}↦X_{t_{λ,i}} for 1≤i≤d and X_{λ,0}↦[(p^{1/p^∞})^{q_λ}]/(X_{t_{λ,1}}⋯X_{t_{λ,r_λ}}) (CK leave the formulas implicit; they follow from the presentation (5.19.2)). For proper 𝔛, compose with the identification (5.43.2) of global-crystalline (CK Corollary 5.43).

proofSteps: By proper-perfectness (CK Corollary 4.20) and global-crystalline (CK Corollary 5.43, whose freeness assertion rests on Beilinson, On the crystalline period map (arXiv:1111.3316v4), §1.18, Theorem), RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris) is a perfect complex over A_cris whose cohomology modules are finite free after inverting p. Hence its base change to B_dR⁺ is derived ξ-complete with finite free cohomology. The finite freeness is not imported from AI.6 canonical deformation.

By CK Remark 5.24, (5.24.1) (Beilinson, (1.11.1); CR.5), the map (5.23.2) is an isomorphism after ⊗^L O_C/p; both RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris)⊗^L_{A_cris}O_C and RΓ_logdR(𝔛/O_C) are perfect over O_C, hence derived p-complete, so RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris)⊗^L_{A_cris}O_C≃RΓ_logdR(𝔛/O_C). By bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings ((6.2.5), (6.2.6)), RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺) is derived ξ-complete with reduction RΓ_dR(X_C^ad/C).

By the square (6.5.7) of bdr-comparison-map, the reduction modulo ξ of the map is RΓ_logdR(𝔛/O_C)⊗_{O_C}C→RΓ_dR(X_C^ad/C). This is an isomorphism: coherent cohomology of the proper formal scheme and of its adic generic fibre agree after inverting p, and Ω^j_{𝔛/O_C,log}[1/p] is the sheaf of continuous differentials of the generic fibre. CK use this without citation; it is the statement taken from AdicSpacesPartII:R3. By derived Nakayama for ξ (E4/mod-ideal-detection, AI.5) the map is an isomorphism; this is (6.6.1), and the freeness of the H^i_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺) follows from the first step.

Combine with (5.43.2) of global-crystalline to obtain (6.6.2). The degreewise form is not in the statement of CK Theorem 6.6; it follows from the flatness of B_dR⁺ over A_inf (CK §6.1, by Raynaud–Gruson, Critères de platitude et de projectivité, II.1.4.2.1; AI.0:period-comparison), which gives H^i(RΓ_Ainf(𝔛)⊗^L_{A_inf}B_dR⁺)=H^i_Ainf(𝔛)⊗_{A_inf}B_dR⁺. CK use it in this form in the proof of Theorem 8.7.
The compatibility modulo ξ with (4.18.1) follows from crystalline-de-rham-square (CK Proposition 5.41) and the commutativity of (6.5.7) (CK Theorem 6.6).

fields.statement: Let 𝔛 be proper. Let c: RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺)→RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p)⊗_{Z_p}B_dR⁺ be the map of BMS1 (proof of Theorem 13.1) supplied by AI.6 canonical deformation; it becomes an isomorphism after ⊗_{B_dR⁺}B_dR, the identification (6.7.1), and is not asserted to be an isomorphism over B_dR⁺. Then the diagram of CK Proposition 6.8 commutes: the composite of bdr-comparison-map’s (6.5.1), of c and of the isomorphism RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p)⊗^L_{Z_p}B_dR⁺≃RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,A_inf,X)⊗^L_{A_inf}B_dR⁺ induced by (2.3.2) equals the composite of the isomorphism RΓ_logcrys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_cris)≃RΓ_Ainf(𝔛)⊗^L_{A_inf}A_cris ((5.43.2) of global-crystalline, the global form of absolute-crystalline’s (5.40.1), which is the label in CK’s diagram) and the map to RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,A_inf,X)⊗^L_{A_inf}B_dR⁺ induced by Lη_μ→id (BMS1 Lemma 6.10). Consequently, after base change to B_dR, the identification RΓ_Ainf(𝔛)⊗^L_{A_inf}B_dR≃RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p)⊗^L_{Z_p}B_dR obtained from etale-comparison equals the one obtained from bdr-comparison and (6.7.1). If moreover X_C^ad≃X₀⊗̂_K C for a proper smooth adic space X₀ over K, with K as in the hypotheses, then under RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR⁺)≃RΓ_dR(X₀/K)⊗_K B_dR⁺ ((6.2.8), using the canonical K→B_dR⁺) the identification (6.7.1) becomes the de Rham comparison (6.7.2) RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p)⊗_{Z_p}B_dR≃RΓ_dR(X₀/K)⊗_K B_dR; when C is the completion of K̄ it is Gal(K̄/K)-equivariant, recovers Scholze’s comparison isomorphism and is compatible with filtrations (the valuation filtration of B_dR, the Hodge filtration on RΓ_dR(X₀/K) and the trivial filtration on étale cohomology).
proofSteps: (2.3.2)⊗B_dR⁺ is an isomorphism: the cohomology of the cone of (2.3.2) is killed by W(𝔪^♭) (etale-comparison; discussion after CK Theorem 2.3), and φ⁻¹(μ)∈W(𝔪^♭) is a unit of B_dR⁺.

Recall c from BMS1, proof of Theorem 13.1 (AI.6 canonical deformation): for Spa(A,A°) in the basis of CK §6.2 and Ψ large, the perfectoid ∏_Ψ Z_p(1)-cover Spa(A_{Ψ,∞},A⁺_{Ψ,∞}) gives a continuous B_dR⁺-map D_Ψ(A)→B_dR⁺(A⁺_{Ψ,∞}), X_u↦[u^{1/p^∞}] (6.8.2), which intertwines exp(log([ε])·∂/∂log X_u) with the generator γ_u of the u-th copy of Z_p(1). The formula of (5.16.1) then gives maps of complexes Ω^•_{D_Ψ(A)/B_dR⁺}→K_{B_dR⁺(A⁺_{Ψ,∞})}((γ_u−1)_{u∈Ψ}) (6.8.3), whose target computes RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,A_inf,X)⊗^L_{A_inf}B_dR⁺ by the almost purity theorem (AI.3). Passing to the colimit over Ψ, sheafifying and taking cohomology gives the composite f of c with (2.3.2).

Extend the construction of (6.8.3) to the étale basis of CK §6.2 and to the data (Ψ,Ξ) of CK §6.3, with the cover that adjoins p-power roots of the X_u (u∈Ψ) and of the X_a (a∈Ξ). By (6.2.7) and (6.3.12) of bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings both variants give the same f. CK say that the remaining modifications are mild; they have to be carried out here, so a local comparison for non-unit coordinates is constructed in this node.

Since f is now built in the setting of CK §6.3 by the same pattern as (5.40.1) (absolute-crystalline; the map of (5.16.1)), the proposition reduces to the commutativity of the square of rings (6.8.4): D_{Σ,Λ}→D_{Ψ,Ξ}(A)→B_dR⁺(A⁺_{Ψ,Ξ,∞}), by (6.5.5) of bdr-comparison-map and (6.8.2), equals D_{Σ,Λ}→A_cris(R_{Σ,Λ,∞})→B_dR⁺(A⁺_{Ψ,Ξ,∞}), by (5.38.1) of all-coordinates-map and (5.36.1). Check it modulo ξⁿ, then on D_{j_{λ₀}}, then, the target being a Q-algebra, on (A□_{Σ,Λ}⊗_{A_inf}A_cris⁰)⊗_{Z[Q]}Z[P_{λ₀}]: both maps send X_τ to the unit [X_τ^{1/p^∞}] for τ=σ∈Σ and τ=(λ,i), 1≤i≤d (CK Proposition 6.8).
The statement over B_dR follows by inverting ξ, using bdr-comparison ((6.6.2)) and AI.6 canonical deformation’s (6.7.1).

Descended case (CK §6.7): (6.2.8) is BMS1 Remark 13.20 (AI.6 canonical deformation), with the unique continuous lift K→B_dR⁺ of K→C; combined with (6.7.1) it gives (6.7.2). If C is the completion of K̄, then (6.7.2) is Galois equivariant by transport of structure and, by BMS1 Theorem 13.1, recovers the isomorphism of Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 8.4; hence it is compatible with filtrations.

proofSteps: Imported from AI.2 (CK §8.2): for a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module M, the étale realization M_ét is a finitely generated Z_p-module with M⊗_{A_inf}W(C^♭)≃M_ét⊗_{Z_p}W(C^♭) and M⊗_{A_inf}A_inf[1/μ]≃M_ét⊗_{Z_p}A_inf[1/μ] (BMS1 Lemma 4.26); hence M⊗_{A_inf}B_dR≃M_ét⊗_{Z_p}B_dR, and M⊗_{A_inf}B_dR⁺ is a B_dR⁺-lattice in it because M[1/p] is free. Fargues’ theorem (BMS1 Theorem 4.28): (M,φ_M)↦(M_ét, M⊗_{A_inf}B_dR⁺) is an equivalence from A_inf-free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules to pairs (T,Ξ).

Equivariant form (CK §8.3, Proposition 8.4): G acts on A_inf, W(C^♭) and B_dR⁺ compatibly with φ and θ (CK §8.1). A semilinear G-action on M commuting with φ_M is a compatible family of isomorphisms between M and its twists by the elements of G; Fargues’ equivalence is compatible with these twists by transport of structure, so it gives the equivalence with pairs carrying a G-action. CK’s proof is the one sentence that the claim follows from §8.2.

Construction of M(T) (CK §8.5): D_dR(T) and the G-equivariant isomorphism T⊗_{Z_p}B_dR≃D_dR(T)⊗_K B_dR for de Rham T[1/p] are imported (AI.6 canonical deformation for the geometric case (6.7.2); the general formalism of de Rham representations has no supplier among the prerequisites). With the canonical G-equivariant map K→B_dR⁺ of AI.0:period-comparison, D_dR(T)⊗_K B_dR⁺ is a G-stable B_dR⁺-lattice; define M(T) by Proposition 8.4. Functoriality: a G-equivariant Z_p-linear map T→T′ induces D_dR(T)→D_dR(T′), so it carries the lattice into the lattice and is a morphism of pairs.

De Rham realization (CK §8.5): M(T) is A_inf-free, so M(T)⊗_{A_inf,θ}O_C is a free O_C-module and an O_C-lattice in M(T)⊗_{A_inf,θ}C=(M(T)⊗_{A_inf}B_dR⁺)/ξ; this is identified with D_dR(T)⊗_K C through B_dR⁺/ξ=C and K→B_dR⁺→C. All maps are G-equivariant because θ is G-equivariant and (ξ) is G-stable.

L_dR(T) is an O_K-lattice. CK state the functorial O_K-lattice conclusion without an argument. Argument: (D_dR(T)⊗_K C)^G=D_dR(T) because C^G=K (Ax–Sen–Tate; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants), so L_dR(T)=M(T)_dR∩D_dR(T). Choose an O_K-lattice L_0 of D_dR(T). Two O_C-lattices of one finite-dimensional C-vector space are commensurable, so p^N(L_0⊗_{O_K}O_C)⊂M(T)_dR⊂p^{−N}(L_0⊗_{O_K}O_C) for some N, and (L_0⊗_{O_K}O_C)∩D_dR(T)=L_0 because O_C∩K=O_K. Hence p^N L_0⊂L_dR(T)⊂p^{−N}L_0; as O_K is a discrete valuation ring, L_dR(T) is a free O_K-module of rank dim_K D_dR(T)=rank_{Z_p}T. The inclusion L_dR(T)⊗_{O_K}O_C⊂M(T)_dR can be strict (see the tests).

Example 8.6: the de Rham comparison (6.7.2) for X proper and smooth over K, functorial in X, G-equivariant and compatible with filtrations, is imported from AI.6 canonical deformation (Scholze; BMS1 Theorem 13.1 and Remark 13.20). It shows that L^i_ét(X)[1/p] is de Rham and gives (8.6.1). Define L^i_dR(X)=L_dR(L^i_ét(X)); functoriality in X follows from that of (6.7.2) and of T↦L_dR(T). The identification of the étale cohomology of X_{K̄} and of X_C is used as in CK.

Finite Galois extensions: for K′/K finite Galois inside K̄ and G′=Gal(K̄/K′), D_dR for G′ is K′⊗_K D_dR(T) (Galois descent for K′/K), so the lattice D_dR(T)⊗_K B_dR⁺ and the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module M(T) are the same for G and for G′, the G′-action being the restriction. Taking invariants in two stages gives L_dR(T)=(L_dR(T|_{G′}))^{Gal(K′/K)}. CK state this consequence of the definition for L^i_dR(X).

Tate twists (not in CK; they follow from the above): the functor to pairs and D_dR on de Rham representations are compatible with tensor products, so M(T⊗T′)≃M(T)⊗_{A_inf}M(T′) by Proposition 8.4. For T=Z_p(1) with basis ε and t=log[ε], D_dR=K·(t^{−1}⊗ε) and the lattice is ξ^{−1}(Z_p(1)⊗B_dR⁺), which is the pair of A_inf{1}=μ^{−1}(A_inf⊗Z_p(1)) (BMS1 Example 4.24 and the sentence after Remark 4.29; AI.2). Hence M(T(n))≃M(T){n}. Since t/μ=1−μ/2+μ²/3−… in B_dR⁺ and θ(μ)=0, the generator μ^{−1}⊗ε reduces to t^{−1}⊗ε in D_dR(Q_p(1))⊗_K C; so L_dR(Z_p(1))=O_K·(t^{−1}⊗ε), and L_dR(T(n))=L_dR(T)·(t^{−n}⊗ε^{⊗n}) because t^{−n}⊗ε^{⊗n} is G-invariant.

proofSteps: Working locally one may replace t_i by t_i^{±1} for r<i≤d, so 𝔛=𝔛₀⊗̂_{O_K}O_C satisfies the chart hypotheses of CK §1.5. By the Grothendieck comparison theorem and flat base change (CK Remark 4.19; CR.5), H_logdR^j(𝔛/O_C)≃H_logdR^j(𝔛₀/O_K)⊗_{O_K}O_C for j=i and j=i+1, hence H_logdR^j(𝔛₀/O_K)=(H_logdR^j(𝔛/O_C))^{G_K} ((8.7.4)). The passage to invariants uses (O_C)^{G_K}=O_K, that is, the theorem of Ax–Sen–Tate C^{G_K}=K (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants, stated there for K finite over Q_p with the general case in its hypotheses), which CK do not cite.

By freeness-criterion (CK Proposition 7.7) in degrees i and i+1, H_A^i(𝔛) and H_A^{i+1}(𝔛) are A_inf-free; by cohomological-bkf, with the semilinear action of G_K of aomega (API item semilinear) and its compatibility with Frobenius stated there, they are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues G_K-modules in the sense of de-rham-lattice-functor (CK §§8.1, 8.3). By (7.6.2) of degreewise-specializations and the Frobenius-compatibility and G_K-equivariance of etale-comparison, the étale realization of H_A^i(𝔛) is H_ét^i(X_C,Z_p), G_K-equivariantly; so T is Z_p-free.

By etale-bdr-agreement (CK Proposition 6.8), the B_dR-base change of this identification equals the composite of bdr-comparison ((6.6.2)), AI.6 canonical deformation’s identification (6.2.8) (BMS1 Remark 13.20) and the de Rham comparison (6.7.2). Hence the B_dR⁺-lattice H_A^i(𝔛)⊗_{A_inf}B_dR⁺ of T⊗_{Z_p}B_dR is D_dR(T)⊗_K B_dR⁺, with D_dR(T)≃H_dR^i(X_K/K) ((8.6.1)). So H_A^i(𝔛) is an A_inf-free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues G_K-module with étale realization T and B_dR⁺-lattice D_dR(T)⊗_K B_dR⁺, and the characterisation of M(T) in de-rham-lattice-functor (CK Proposition 8.4 and §8.5) gives M(T)≃H_A^i(𝔛), which is (8.7.3).

Under this identification, by the compatibility modulo ξ in bdr-comparison (CK Theorem 6.6) and the sentence after (6.2.8), the identifications of M(T)⊗_{A_inf,θ}C and of H_A^i(𝔛)⊗_{A_inf,θ}C with H_dR^i(X_C^ad/C) agree. Since H_A^{i+1}(𝔛) is free, (7.6.3) gives H_A^i(𝔛)⊗_{A_inf,θ}O_C=H_logdR^i(𝔛/O_C) inside H_dR^i(X_C^ad/C). Taking G_K-invariants and using the first step gives (8.7.2) (CK Theorem 8.7).
Model independence: by de-rham-lattice-functor, L_dR(T)=L^i_dR(X_K) depends only on T with its G_K-action, hence only on the generic fibre (CK Example 8.6, (8.6.2)).

fields.statement: For a p-completely smooth O_K-algebra R, let 𝔖^(−1) be the copy of 𝔖 containing 𝔖 via φ_𝔖 and embedded in A_inf by g. Define D̂_tw(R)=gr⁰TC⁻(R/𝕊[z];Z_p)≃gr⁰TP(R/𝕊[z];Z_p), by unfolding π₀ from the quasiregular semiperfectoid site as in BMS2 §§11.1–11.2; here O_K is an 𝕊[z]-algebra through z↦π. It is a (p,u)-complete E∞-𝔖^(−1)-algebra, the algebra structure coming from π₀TC⁻(O_K/𝕊[z];Z_p)=𝔖^(−1), in which the variable z of 𝕊[z] is the coefficient variable u; its Frobenius linearization is invertible after φ(E)-inversion. The AI.7 relative trace targets supply the relative spectra, filtration, unfolding and coefficient computations.
proofSteps: Import the AI.7 relative trace targets’ relative THH/TC⁻/TP computation and its quasisyntomic descent, using the map z↦π: the cyclotomic structure on THH(−/𝕊[z]) (BMS2 Construction 11.5), the coefficient computation BMS2 Proposition 11.10, and evenness and the sheaf property on quasiregular semiperfectoid O_K-algebras, BMS2 Proposition 11.11, which rests on BMS2 Theorem 7.2.

Apply BMS2 Corollary 11.12, with the relative TC⁻(−/𝕊[z];Z_p) and with gr⁰ of the filtration obtained by unfolding from quasiregular semiperfectoid algebras; on smooth algebras this is not π₀, and absolute TC⁻ carries no 𝔖-module structure. Its proof uses, besides §§11.1–11.2, the absolute results BMS2 Theorem 1.17 for part (2), Theorem 1.8 for part (1) and Theorem 1.10 for part (3), with BMS2 Corollary 11.8 and Lemma 11.6 for base change in 𝕊[z]; all belong to AI.7 relative traces. Part (4) is deduced from part (1) because 𝔖^(−1)→A_inf is a topological direct summand, which is flat-coefficient-extension applied to g.

proofSteps: Use the AI.7 relative trace targets’ evenness, acyclicity and cyclotomic extension in BMS2 Proposition 11.15, with Propositions 11.10 and 11.11 and, for the reduction modulo z^{1/p}, Lemma 11.6; the source’s Segal input Corollary 8.18 belongs to AI.7 relative traces.

Apply the unfolding/descent of the proof of BMS2 Theorem 11.2, retaining its relative base and its canonical Frobenius composite; the first display of that proof must be read with TC⁻(A/𝕊[z];Z_p), as in Proposition 11.15 and in the composite display of the same proof.

Compatibility with the Frobenius of D̂_tw, whose verification BMS2 leaves implicit: let Φ:D_𝔖^tr→gr⁰TP be the φ_𝔖-semilinear map of Proposition 11.15 and loc:gr⁰TC⁻→D_𝔖^tr the b-inversion. By construction Φ∘loc is the cyclotomic Frobenius φ^{hT}:gr⁰TC⁻→gr⁰TP. The semilinear descent Frobenius is F=loc∘can^{-1}∘Φ, so Φ∘F=φ^{hT}∘can^{-1}∘Φ, and φ^{hT}∘can^{-1} is the Frobenius endomorphism of gr⁰TP≃D̂_tw.

Invertibility after E: the linearized Frobenius of D̂_tw is invertible after inverting φ_𝔖(E) (twisted-trace, BMS2 Corollary 11.12(4)); φ_𝔖 is finite free of rank p (R07.4/bk-coefficient-rings), hence faithfully flat, so the cone of the linearized Frobenius of D_𝔖^tr vanishes after inverting E.

proofSteps: For quasiregular semiperfectoid quasisyntomic O_K-algebras S use BS22 Proposition 15.7 (AI.7 relative traces, with the prismatic input PR.3/bms2-comparison): the cyclotomic Frobenius on π₀TP(S/𝕊[z];Z_p) is the Frobenius of a δ-structure; the universal property of Δ_{S/𝔖} as initial object of the prismatic site of S over 𝔖 (BS22 Theorem 15.2(1)) gives a map Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}→π₀TP(S/𝕊[z];Z_p); and this map identifies the target with the Nygaard completion, compatibly with Nygaard filtrations (relative-nygaard-filtration). Both checks are made after the (p,u)-completed base change 𝔖→W(k₀)[[u^{1/p^∞}]], where relative THH becomes absolute THH of S⟨π^{1/p^∞}⟩ (BMS2 Corollary 11.8) and BS22 Theorem 13.1 applies.

Under this identification and the canonical map, π_{2i}TC⁻(S/𝕊[z];Z_p) is the i-th step Fil^i_N of the Nygaard filtration of π₀TP(S/𝕊[z];Z_p) and b corresponds to E (twisted-trace: can(b)=Eσ). Hence π₀(TC⁻(S/𝕊[z];Z_p)[1/b]) is the union of the E^{−i}Fil^i_N, and the relative Frobenius φ_{S/𝔖}, which maps Fil^i_N into E^iΔ_{S/𝔖}, induces ring maps π₀(TC⁻(S/𝕊[z];Z_p)[1/b])→Δ_{S/𝔖}, n/E^i↦φ_{S/𝔖}(n)/E^i, natural in S. They commute with the Frobenius endomorphisms: the extended cyclotomic Frobenius of trace-descent is this ring map followed by Δ_{S/𝔖}→Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}, x↦x⊗1.

Unfold over the quasisyntomic site of R: BMS2 Proposition 11.15 for the trace side (trace-descent), and BS22 Theorem 15.3, first display, for RΓ_Δ(X/𝔖)≃RΓ(X_qsyn,Δ_{−/𝔖}). For i at least the dimension of R the map φ:Fil^i_N→E^iΔ_{−/𝔖} induces an equivalence on RΓ(X_qsyn,−), because both sides are complete for compatible filtrations and the graded pieces agree by BS22 Theorem 15.3 (relative-nygaard-graded-pieces, leta-frobenius-factorisation). So the colimit over i stabilises and the ring maps of the previous step induce the equivalence (a). This is the argument of BS22 §15.2, whose reference to [BMS19, Proposition 11.5] is to BMS2 Proposition 11.15.
Multiplicativity in (a) is not printed in BS22: it holds because the equivalence is induced on derived global sections by the ring maps of the second step.

(b) is not proved. Towards it the listed inputs give only this. The maps of the first step come from a universal property, so their base change along 𝔖→W(k₀)[[u^{1/p^∞}]]→A_inf is the map given by the same universal property over the base-changed prism; this is how BS22 reduces to Theorem 13.1. PR.6/comparison-uniqueness (BS22 Theorem 18.2) applies to the comparison isomorphisms between AΩ, the absolute trace complex and φ_A^*Δ_{−/A_inf} as functors on all p-completely smooth O_C-algebras (BS22 Theorems 13.1 and 17.2, PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison); it applies neither to functors defined only on smooth O_K-algebras nor over A_inf⊗̂_𝔖A_inf, which is not a perfect prism. Equalities of maps over 𝔖 can be tested after extension along f by flat-coefficient-extension.

proofSteps: Import PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (BS22 Theorem 15.3) for the prismatic statement and AI.1’s filtered décalage/Beilinson connective cover (BMS2 Proposition 5.8).

For the trace complex follow BMS2 Remark 11.17. The AI.7 relative trace targets supply the filtered map from the Nygaard filtration of D̂_tw (BMS2 Remark 11.14) to the E-adic filtration of D_𝔖^tr: the restriction of the Frobenius to the i-th Nygaard step is divisible by E^i because v^i=E^i/b^i in π_*TC⁻(O_K/𝕊[z];Z_p)[1/b], and E is a non-zero-divisor on π_*TC⁻(S/𝕊[z];Z_p) for quasiregular semiperfectoid S. Its source is connective for the Beilinson t-structure as in BMS2 Corollary 7.10(1). That it is a connective cover is checked after extension to A_inf, where it is BMS2 Proposition 9.10; equivalences are detected there because 𝔖→A_inf is topologically free (flat-coefficient-extension).

That the two factorisations correspond is not stated in the sources. Under trace-prismatic-agreement the filtered Frobenius of the previous step goes to the prismatic one: on quasiregular semiperfectoid algebras both send an element n of the i-th Nygaard step to E^i times the class n/E^i. The factorisation of a filtered map from a Beilinson-connective object through the connective cover is unique (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation).

proofSteps: (a) Import AΩ_R≃φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf} with its Frobenius compatibility from PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison (BS22 Theorem 17.2, Remark 17.3). The comparison map intertwines the two Hodge–Tate structure maps η; BS22 leaves the reduction to the completed torus R = O_C[x^{±1}]^∧ to the reader, and PR.6/theta-theta-tilde-square records it. By BS22 Lemma 17.4 a multiplicative map that intertwines the maps η induces an isomorphism of the cohomology algebras of the θ̃ reductions with their Bockstein differentials, both identified with (Ω^*_{R/O_C},d) through the universal property of the de Rham complex; so compatibility with dt on O_C⟨t⟩ and dlog t on O_C⟨t^{±1}⟩ is a consequence of compatibility on H⁰, not an additional condition.

(a) Apply PR.6/comparison-uniqueness (BS22 Theorem 18.2) over the perfect A_inf prism (A_inf,(ξ̃)): the pair formed by prismatic cohomology and η has no nontrivial endomorphism among pairs (G,η) with G a symmetric monoidal functor on all p-completely smooth O_C-algebras; Frobenius compatibility is not an extra hypothesis of that uniqueness theorem. This step needs the comparison as a morphism of pairs (G,η) of symmetric monoidal functors, hence its naturality in R and its multiplicativity.

(b) is not proved. A possible route: for the θ de Rham map, compare the two factorisations of Frobenius through Lη_{ξ̃} (that of AΩ in BMS1 and BS22 Theorem 15.3), noting that BMS1 Theorem 14.1 deduces its de Rham comparison from the A_cris comparison and mentions the route through Lη only as an alternative; for the crystalline maps use PR.1 crystalline/base change and AI.4’s actual PD maps and check on PD/Koszul generators; for the Breuil–Kisin and trace maps use ainf-base-change, trace-prismatic-agreement and the AI.7 relative trace comparison map; AI.5 and AI.6 supply the generic étale/B_dR square.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 11.16, p.307 (Publ. math. IHÉS 129)
sourceIssues.printed: The obstruction to functorial Frobenius descent is illustrated for general K by an elliptic j-invariant outside W(k)[π^p].
sourceIssues.correction: A descent along φ of the projection for A=O_K is a quotient 𝔖/J with φ(J)𝔖=(E). If no such J exists, which is so whenever p does not divide the degree e of E (in particular for K unramified, where moreover W(k)[π^p]=O_K and no elliptic curve as described exists), there is no descent already for A=O_K, for a different reason. If it exists, J=ker θ, 𝔖/J≅W(k)[π^p], O_K is free of rank p over it, and the elliptic-curve argument applies.

More generally p∤e obstructs coefficient-ideal descent already for O_K. The conclusion about absence of functorial descent survives with these separate cases.

links.reason: Finite Witt coherence, polynomial inclusions, almost ideals and étale base change precede both AΩ and relative de Rham–Witt.
The canonical B_dR⁺ deformation prefix moves down here. CP.3 imports it and retains subsequent rational comparison diagrams and filtered enhancements.
The relative sphere-polynomial trace input needed for Breuil–Kisin descent moves here; RT.6 imports it for broader trace applications.
Rational semistable assembly imports the log crystalline, étale and B_dR maps.
Generic A_inf module and proper smooth torsion inputs are owned here; CP.5 imports the geometric statements.
Semistable torsion and adjacent-degree model-independent lattices are owned here.
